briefs.title: Asteroid dodger
briefs.brief: A small arcade game: the player steers a ship left and right along the bottom of the screen while asteroids fall from the top at increasing speed. Score goes up with survival time. Hitting an asteroid ends the game on a game-over screen showing the score; a key restarts. Keep the best score across page reloads.
briefs.followUp: Add a shield power-up that occasionally falls from the top. Catching it makes the next asteroid hit harmless (show that the shield is active).

briefs.title: Cannon vs tower
briefs.brief: A physics game: a cannon on the left fires heavy balls (aim with up/down, fire with space) at a tower of stacked wooden blocks standing on a platform on the right. Blocks must fall and tumble realistically. You win when every block has fallen off the platform; show the number of shots used.
briefs.followUp: Add a second level with a taller, wider tower that loads after you win the first.

conditions.moonstage: Build it with Moonstage, a browser game runtime with a CLI. The CLI is `{cli}` (equivalent to `npx moonstage`). Work in `{dir}`. You know nothing else about Moonstage; find out what you need from the CLI.
conditions.freestyle: Build it as a single self-contained HTML file (inline JavaScript and CSS, no external libraries or network requests) at `{dir}/index.html`.

protocol: First build the game and make sure it works. Then copy the finished version to `{dir}-v1` (a sibling directory) so it can be compared. Then apply the follow-up request in `{dir}` and make sure it still works. Do not ask questions; make reasonable choices. Finish with a short report: what you built, how you verified it, anything that did not work.

campaigns.title: Brick breaker campaign
campaigns.brief: A brick breaker: a paddle at the bottom (left/right to move) bounces a ball into rows of bricks at the top. Bricks break when hit and add to the score. Missing the ball costs one of three lives; at zero lives a game-over screen shows the score, and a key restarts. Clearing every brick shows a win screen.
followUps: Some bricks drop a power-up capsule when broken. Catching it with the paddle makes the paddle twice as wide for 10 seconds.
Add a second level with a different brick layout that loads after the first is cleared, keeping score and lives. The win screen now appears after the last level.
Keep the five best scores across page reloads and show them on the game-over and win screens.
Pressing P pauses and resumes the game; while paused nothing moves and a PAUSED overlay shows.
A rare power-up splits the ball into three. A life is lost only when the last ball is missed.

campaignProtocol: Build the base game and make sure it works, then copy it to `{dir}-step0`. Then apply each follow-up in order; after follow-up N works, copy the project to `{dir}-stepN`. Every follow-up must keep every earlier feature working. Do not ask questions; make reasonable choices. Finish with a short report: what you built at each step, how you verified it, and anything that broke along the way.
